xian-shiyou-university.h: Xi'an Shiyou University in a nutshell

blocks.x: Xi'an Shiyou University (西安石油大学, pinyin Xīān Shíyóu Dàxué, abbreviated XSYU) is a university in Xi'an, also known in English as Xi'an Petroleum University. What sets it apart is its focus: it describes itself as Northwest China's only multi-disciplinary college that is characterised by petroleum and petrochemicals, and it counts among five famous petroleum universities in the country. Students can follow a complete training path here, from undergraduate study through postgraduate work to a doctorate.

Figures from June 2018 give a sense of scale. The Yanta, Mingde (South) and Huyi campuses together cover about 55 acres. The university employs more than 1,700 faculty members, among them more than 1,200 full-time teachers. Enrolment includes over 16,000 undergraduates, over 750 international students, and two groups of advanced students: more than 1,900 full-time graduate students plus over 1,400 full-time postgraduate students.

The roots go back to the Northwest Petroleum Industry College, founded in 1951. By 1958 it had become Xi'an Petroleum Institute. In 1969 the college was shut and its site converted into a factory, and it reopened as Xi'an Petroleum Institute in 1980. A change of ownership came in 2000: the China National Petroleum Corporation handed it over to the central and local governments, and day-to-day management passed mainly to the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government. The present name, Xi'an Petroleum University, was adopted in 2003.

As of July 2018 the university has over 1,700 faculty members, including nearly 600 with senior titles and more than 1,200 full-time teachers. Four special academicians work there, along with over 40 second- and third-level professors. More than 600 teachers hold doctorates, and over 460 staff are doctoral supervisors or master tutors.

Recognition is wide. Nearly 40 people are state-recognised experts with outstanding contributions, or draw the special allowances that the China State Council pays to selected experts, or are national model teachers or national outstanding teachers, or belong to the national "National Talents" and "Thousand Talents Plan" schemes. Other honours come from Shaanxi Province: its "Three Qin Scholars" positions, the "Hundred Talents Program", the "Three-Five Talent Project", the Shaanxi Provincial Teachers' Morals award, and titles such as advanced worker, outstanding teacher and famous teacher. The Ministry of Education's "New Century Excellent Talents" programme is also represented. In all, more than 80 people on the staff hold such honours.
The four special academicians are:
Guowei Zhang, of the Chinese Academy of Sciences
Helin Li, Pingya Luo and Xinyi Gu, of the Chinese Academy of Engineering

By the end of 2017 the university had five national-level specialty programmes, five Shaanxi "first-class professional" construction projects and seven Shaanxi "first-class professional" cultivation projects. Five of its programmes were pilots of the national "excellent engineer education training" scheme, ten are Shaanxi specialty programmes, and five are Shaanxi famous-brand majors.

The awards count is long. For teaching achievement, it has won two national second prizes, 22 provincial awards and 10 awards from the China Petroleum Education Association. On courses, it has two provincial-level online open courses, 19 provincial quality courses, 13 provincial boutique resource-sharing courses and 15 provincial renovation-and-upgrading resource-sharing courses. Teaching infrastructure is substantial. Shaanxi has recognised 21 teaching teams at the university and 15 Talent Training Model Innovation Experimental Zones. There are also two Shaanxi Virtual Simulation Experimental Teaching Centers and 13 Shaanxi Experimental Teaching Demonstration Centers. On top of that come 13 industry-university cooperation and education projects supported by the Ministry of Education.

The five national-level specialty programmes are Computer Science and Technology, Mechanical Design and Automation, Measurement and Control Technology, Petroleum Engineering and Resource Exploration Engineering. For practical training, the university also has a national-level off-campus practice education base for university students: the Engineering Practice Education Center, operated jointly by Xi'an Petroleum University and China Petroleum Changqing Petrochemical Company.

By 10 June 2014, XSYU had built relations with 43 universities and institutions across Kazakhstan, Russia, Germany, Australia, Britain, Canada and the United States. Several formal pathways exist for students:
a China-US Talent Training Program on a "1+2+1" model, set up with 13 American universities
the "2+2 Undergraduate Double Degree" programme, run together with Korean, Russian and American universities
the "4+1" and "4+2" master's programmes and a doctoral scholarship programme, with partners in the United States, Britain and Germany
"exchange student projects" involving Russian and American universities
short-term overseas projects in summer and winter, in France, Germany, Britain, the United States and other countries

The university also teaches international students in China: more than 350 from 25 countries at the time. In 2012 the Ministry of Education approved it to host Chinese government scholarship students and also approved a Chinese government scholarship scheme for independently recruited Russian students.

In June 2014 the school ran 20 key laboratories or engineering technology research centers at provincial or ministerial level or above, plus 5 at school level. One of them is the National Engineering Laboratory for developing and exploring low permeability oil and gas fields.

Seven national awards have come to the university. Four were National Science and Technology Progress Awards, two were National Invention Awards, and the last was a National Science and Technology Research Achievement Award.
Three addresses matter for applicants:
The main campus is in Yanta District. Its street address is Electronic Road No.2 (the eastern section), number 18, in the city of Xi'an, Shaanxi Province (陕西省西安市雁塔区电子二路东段18号).
The South campus is also in Yanta District, at 18 East Zhanba Road (陕西省西安市雁塔区丈八东路).
The Huyi campus is further out, in Wuzhu Town of Huyi District, inside the Fengjing Industrial Park; the address is 18 Fengjing Avenue (陕西省西安市鄠邑区五竹镇沣京工业园沣京大道18号).
The Chinese author Chen Zhongshi is one of the university's alumni.
Daily life depends so much on the city outside the campus gates that it is worth knowing Xi'an's setting, weather, transport and economy before you arrive.

Xi'an sits on the Guanzhong Plain in south-central Shaanxi province, on a flood plain formed by eight surrounding rivers and streams. Along the south, the Qin Mountains (Qinling) rise at the city's edge, and on the north side lie the banks of the Wei River. Among the five sacred Taoist mountains, Hua Shan is about 100 km (62 mi) east of the city, while the Loess Plateau lies not far to the north.

The region's reputation goes back to the start of the Han dynasty. Zhang Liang, the Chief of Staff, urged the emperor Liu Bang to make Guanzhong his capital, arguing that the plain lies behind Mount Xiao and Hangu Pass and links Long (Gansu) with Shu (Sichuan), an "iron castle" stretching a thousand miles and and as rich in harvests as the "nation of heaven", in the words of the original 关中左崤函，右陇蜀，沃野千里，此所谓金城千里，天府之国也. Ever since, Guanzhong has also been called the "Nation of the Heaven".

Xi'an has a temperate climate affected by the East Asian monsoon. Under the Köppen system it falls on the border between humid subtropical and hot-summer humid continental (Cwa/Dwa). In the Wei River valley, summers are hot and humid, winters cold and dry, and springs and autumns dry. Most rain arrives between July and late October. Snow sometimes falls in winter but seldom lies for long. March and April bring frequent dust storms as the city warms up fast, and summer often has short, frequent thunderstorms.

Averaged over 24 hours, temperatures begin near freezing in January and peak at 27.0 °C (80.6 °F) in July; the mean for the whole year is 14.08 °C (57.3 °F). Since 1951 the coldest reading was -20.6 °C (-5 °F) on 11 January 1955, and the hottest at the current Jinghe station was 42.3 °C (108 °F) on 15 July 2025. Another station logged an even higher 42.9 °C (109 °F) on 17 June 2006. An unofficial low of -25.0 °C (-13 °F) was noted in January 1930 at a different weather station, in the northern suburbs.

xian-shiyou-university.h: The home of China's standard time

blocks.x: Near Xi'an is the National Time Service Center (NTSC), part of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Its roots lie in the Shaanxi Astronomical Observatory, set up in 1966. In 1975 the People's Republic's Geodetic Origin Report stated that, to reduce bias in measurement as far as possible, the Geodetic Origin should be in central mainland China, and the choice fell on Lintong (临潼), a town near Xi'an. Chinese Standard Time (CST) has been set by NTSC since 1986. The centre works mainly on services and research for time and frequency: it generates and maintains the national standard time scale and sends out time and frequency signals. During the 1970s and 1980s it built its own standard time scales for universal time and atomic time, and ways to broadcast them by LF and HF radio, which by and large met needs ranging from scientific research to the national economy.

The Seventh National Census of 2020 recorded a permanent (hukou) population of 12,952,907 in the city. Men were 51.07% and women 48.93%. By age, 15.65% were 0-14, 68.33% were 15-59, 16.02% were over 60 and 10.9% were over 65. The OECD estimated the Xi'an metropolitan area at 12.9 million people in 2010, 5,740,000 of whom were urban.

Many parts of Xi'an are easy to walk. Pedestrians have been given underpasses and overpasses, for safety and convenience, in many commercial, residential and educational zones. The shopping and entertainment area around the Bell Tower is a prime example.

Bike sharing began in 2013 and now runs 52,000 bikes, with over 200,000 people using them on a typical day. Taxis are plentiful, yet many residents still commute by bus; there are 270 official municipal routes, run with a fleet of over 7,800 vehicles, and together they carry over 4 million passengers on an average day, and a fast-growing subway system adds over 1.5 million commuters daily. With more than 2 million registered cars in the city, congestion is a frequent urban problem.

The first line opened to the public was Line 2, on 16 September 2011, with operations starting on 28 September 2011. It runs north to south through the city, between North Railway Station and Weiqu Nan, over 19.9 kilometers (12.4 miles) and 17 stations. Line 1 followed on 15 September 2013, a west-east line of 19 stations between Houweizhai and Fangzhicheng. Line 3 runs from Baoshuiqu in the northeast to Yuhuazhai in the southwest, and opened on 8 November 2016. Line 4 runs roughly parallel to Line 2 on its east side, apart from the northern parts, from Hangtianxincheng in the south up to Beikezhan (Beiguangchang), the North Square of the North Railway Station, and it opened to the public on 26 December 2018. Line 5 opened on 28 December 2020 and has 31 stations, from Matengkong to Chuangxingang, over 41.6 kilometers.
Line 16 opened on 27 June 2023. It is 15.03 kilometers long, with 9 stations from Qinchuangyuanzhongxin to Shijingli. Four more lines, including an extension of Line 1, are being built.

The subway reaches some of the city's best-known sights: Banpo Museum (Line 1, Banpo Station), Bell and Drum Tower and the Fortifications of Xi'an (both on Line 2), Line 4 stops at the Daminggong National Heritage Park, Lines 3 and 4 at the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, and Lines 2, 3 and 4 at the Shaanxi History Museum, among other attractions.
First trains on Lines 1, 2, 3 and 4 leave at 6:00. Last departures are at 23:00 on Lines 3 and 4, 23:30 on Line 1 and 23:50 on Line 2.
A fire broke out on 30 December 2008 and was put out within an hour, with every worker got out safely. Another fire started on 2 January, sixty-six hours later, at a different station on Line 2.

Xi'an North railway station, a few miles north of the city centre, handles the high-speed trains of the Zhengzhou-Xi'an High-Speed Railway, which forms part of the Xuzhou-Lanzhou high-speed railway. Work on that railway started on 25 September 2005 and it opened for service on 6 February 2010, and it left air travel between Zhengzhou and Xi'an uncompetitive: within 48 days of regular high-speed service starting, all passenger flights between the two cities had been suspended. Building of the station started on 19 September 2008 and it opened on 11 January 2011. When it opened, its 34 platforms made it the largest railway station in Northwest China. It is also served by the Datong-Xi'an high-speed railway, which connects with Beijing North, as well as the Xi'an-Chengdu and Yinchuan-Xi'an high-speed railways.

Xi'an railway station stands just north of the walled city and is the main hub for conventional trains in Shaanxi Province. It occupies a site of 597,000 square meters (6,430,000 square feet) and contains 6 passenger platforms and 11 passenger tracks, and it handles 112 services and 80 000 people daily. Direct trains run to Beijing, Zhengzhou, Lanzhou, Baoji and Mount Hua, among other places.

Two large stations, Xi'an South and Xi'an East, are being built for new high-speed lines such as the Wuhan-Xi'an HSR and the Xi'an-Chongqing HSR. Four other stations serve the city: Fangzhicheng, Sanmincun, Yinzhen and Xi'an West.

Xi'an Xianyang International Airport (code XIY) is the main airport and the largest in northwest China. The airport stands 25 miles northwest of the centre of Xi'an, while the centre of Xianyang is 8 miles southwest of it. The main carriers are Hainan Airlines, China Southern Airlines and China Eastern Airlines. Terminal 3 and the second runway opened on 3 May 2012, and Terminal 5, started in 2022, was completed in September 2024.
Besides connections to most Chinese cities, the airport flies to several major international destinations, such as Tokyo, Seoul, London, Paris and Sydney.

Xi'an became a main target of accelerated attention under the China Western Development policy, particularly aerospace, energy, advanced materials, chemical engineering and information technology. Between 1997 and 2006 the output value of the city's modern service industry grew by 13 percent a year on average, against 0.74 percent for traditional services, from US$8.113 billion at the start to US$25.85 billion at the end.

In 2020 the Globalization and World Cities Research Network ranked Xi'an a Beta- (global second tier) city, and the Global Financial Centres Index put it among the world's top 100 financial centers that year.

Equipment manufacturing, tourism and service outsourcing are important. Annual output from manufacturing was RMB 36.5 billion, which is 44.5 percent of the city's total. Xi'an is also one of China's four ancient capitals, and cultural sites such as the Famen Temple, the City Wall of Xi'an and the Terracotta Army make tourism a major industry too. Visitors to Xi'an passed 300 million in 2019, and the income they brought was RMB 314.6 billion. On average, revenue increases 36.4 percent a year, and foreign-exchange earnings, at 530 million in 2009, are rising by about 35.8 percent.

Xi'an was among the first service outsourcing cities in China and has over 800 firms in that field, whose output value topped RMB 23 billion in 2008. From a base of 60,000, employment in the sector doubled between 1997 and 2006, and computer consulting doubled from 16,000 to 32,000. Because software outsourcing matters so much, the city planned a Software New Town, due for completion in 2015 with 30 billion RMB of investment. Lighting equipment and automobile parts are other big exports, while mechanical and electrical products are the main imports. The United States is Xi'an's largest international trade partner.

Covering about thirty-five square miles, the Xi'an International Trade and Logistics Park was conceived as a model of logistics-based urbanization, and it works as a big inland container port and rail hub. More China-Europe Freight Train (CEFT) services start or end in Xi'an than in any other city.
Xi'an's main industrial zone is its Economic and Technological Development Zone. Separately, China's largest landfill site, Jiangcungou in Xi'an, stayed in use until 2019.

The growing economy supports a software industry, and Xi'an is a pioneer of software in China. Within the Xi'an Hi-Tech Industries Development Zone (XDZ), the Xi'an Software Park had attracted 106,000 employees and over 1,085 corporations by 2012. One account says the city draws on a huge pool of low-cost talent from the area's 100 universities, taking on around 3,000 computer graduates each year at approximately $120 a month, which is half what the same job pays in Beijing.

The Xi'an Aerospace Science and Technology Industrial Base was jointly established in November 2006 by the city of Xi'an and the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation. The base has concentrated on civil space industry from the start, among them new materials, solar photovoltaics, equipment manufacturing, and software and service outsourcing.

Beyond the core area, the base will extend across Xi'an and the Guanzhong area, with an expansion zone covering other parts of Northwest and Southwest China. The target for 2012 was total industry output of 2.8 billion US dollars. Plans also called for 5 to 8 products able to compete globally, and about 10 to 20 own brands carrying intellectual property rights.

In 2008, after launching the first aerospace centre in Shanghai, the PRC began building another civil aerospace centre in Shaanxi province. On 26 December 2007 planning for the Xi'an National Civil Aerospace Industrial Base won approval from the State Development and Reform Commission. The base, covering an area of 23 km2 (8.9 sq mi), will work on civil-use technologies: satellites, energies, IT and new materials among them.
Several well-known professional teams used to play in the city before relocating:
Shaanxi National Power, in the Chinese Jia-A League, moved to Ningbo and became Ningbo National Power in 2004
Shaanxi Baorong Chanba, in the Chinese Football Association Super League, moved to Guiyang and became Guizhou Renhe in 2012
Shaanxi Dongsheng, in the Chinese Basketball Association, moved to Foshan and became Foshan Dralions in 2010

For a prospective student the picture is clear. XSYU offers a specialist education in petroleum and related fields in a large, historic and well-connected city with a growing technology and aerospace economy, hot summers, cold dry winters and metro lines that reach the main sights.
Xi'an Shiyou University lists 56 programs for international students on this site: 18 bachelor, 31 master's, 5 doctoral, 2 non-degree programs.

By language of instruction: 37 taught in Chinese, 19 taught in English. English-taught programs do not require Chinese to start; for Chinese-taught programs you normally need an HSK certificate at the level the program sets.
Annual tuition for bachelor programs ranges from CNY 15,500 to CNY 18,500 (median CNY 15,500), according to the university's published fee table.
Annual tuition for master's programs ranges from CNY 18,500 to CNY 21,500 (median CNY 18,500), according to the university's published fee table.
Annual tuition for doctoral programs ranges from CNY 28,000 to CNY 30,000 (median CNY 28,000), according to the university's published fee table.

53 of these programs are listed as open to Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) applicants, which means a CSC award can cover tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend and medical insurance for eligible students.
English-taught degree programs (15):
Artificial Intelligence
Business Administration
Civil Engineering
Computer Science and Technology
Electrical Engineering
Geological Resources and Geological Engineering
Geology
Industrial Economics
Materials Science and Engineering
Mechanical Engineering
Offshore Oil and Gas Engineering
Petroleum Engineering
Petroleum and Natural Gas Engineering
Power Engineering and Engineering Thermophysics
Resource Exploration Engineering
The university has not published an application window that we could confirm yet. Intake dates change every year; a CAS advisor can confirm the current window for your program before you apply.

International students at Chinese universities can fund their studies through the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), provincial and city government scholarships, and university scholarships. Each has its own application route and timetable, and some are applied for through your home country's Chinese embassy rather than the university.

xian-shiyou-university.h: How to apply, step by step

blocks.x: The process below is the general route for international degree applicants to Chinese universities. Xi'an Shiyou University may add its own forms, interviews or deadlines, which a CAS advisor confirms before you apply.
Choose a program and check its language of instruction, duration and annual tuition on the Programs tab.

Check the admission requirements: a valid foreign passport, good health, and the right previous qualification (high-school graduation for a bachelor's degree, a bachelor's degree for a master's, a master's degree for a doctorate).
Bachelor's applicants take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) and send the result with the application.
Prove language ability: an HSK certificate for Chinese-taught programs, or English test results (for example IELTS or TOEFL) for English-taught programs, unless you studied in English.
Prepare certified transcripts and diplomas, a physical examination form, a police clearance certificate and a study plan or personal statement where the program asks for them.
Apply online through the university's international student system, or let CAS prepare and submit the application for you, and pay the application fee.
After admission you receive an admission notice and a JW202 or JW201 form, which you take to the Chinese embassy or consulate to apply for an X1 (long-term study) visa.
Travel to Xi'an, register at Xi'an Shiyou University by the date in the admission notice, and convert your entry visa into a residence permit within 30 days of arrival.

Xiamen University, usually shortened to XMU, is a public university in the Siming district of Xiamen, a coastal city in Fujian province. It answers to China's Ministry of Education and belongs to three national schemes created to lift the country's strongest institutions: the Double First-Class initiative, Project 985 and Project 211. In 2017 it was placed in the Class A group of the Double First-Class plan, the government scheme that aims to build a set of elite Chinese universities into world-class institutions by 2050.

The university opened in 1921 on the initiative of Tan Kah Kee, a patriotic overseas Chinese businessman based in Singapore. It is widely counted among the leading universities of southern China. Its reputation rests on a spread of fields. Economics and management come up most often, followed by law, chemistry, mathematics, oceanography, communication and political science, and other descriptions add fine arts and journalism.

For planning purposes, size matters. As of April 2023 more than 45,000 students were enrolled, of whom over 21,000 were undergraduates, more than 19,000 were taking master's degrees and over 5,000 were working on doctorates. That is a large, research-active community, with postgraduates making up more than half of the total.

XMU also looks outward. It has agreements with 263 universities abroad and runs substantial exchanges with 53 of them, and another count puts its exchange and cooperation relationships at more than 300 universities. In July 2014 work began on XMU Malaysia, which made it the first Chinese university to set up a fully independent campus overseas.

The story starts in 1919, when Tan Kah Kee, a Singapore-based expatriate who was a businessman, investor and philanthropist, pledged 4 million dollars to found a new university in Amoy. Amoy is the older romanisation of Xiamen and stayed in use until the 1970s. When the institution opened in 1921 it was tiny, with no more than 20 teachers and just 98 students.

It gained international attention early. At the Sesquicentennial International Exposition held in Philadelphia in 1926, Amoy University was one of five Chinese institutions chosen to present an exhibit on education in China, which meant it was helping to represent the whole national higher education system.

In 1937 Tan handed the running of the university over to the Nationalist government, and it became a national university. The war then interrupted its life on the coast. Fighting reached the coast in the Amoy Operation of 1938, part of the Second Sino-Japanese War, and the university moved temporarily to Changting in western Fujian to keep away from the Japanese advance along the coast. It came back to Xiamen in 1946 and resumed ordinary operations.
In 1952 it was reshaped into a comprehensive university covering both arts and sciences, and in 1963 it was named a key university of China.

Two government funding programmes mark the later stages. In 1995 XMU was chosen for Project 211, which directs extra money to the most promising universities. In 2000 it was added to Project 985, a joint national and local programme that pays for buildings and for recruiting academic staff to strengthen the top universities. The 2017 Class A ranking in the Double First-Class plan followed.

The Malaysian project has its own short timeline. High-level talks between the Chinese and Malaysian governments began in 2011. On 25 January 2013 Malaysia's higher education ministry sent XMU a formal invitation to open a branch campus. The foundation was laid near Kuala Lumpur on 3 July 2014, the institution was established in 2015, and the campus officially opened on 22 February 2016.

In short: founded in 1921, national from 1937, wartime move in 1938, return in 1946, comprehensive in 1952, key university in 1963, Project 211 in 1995, Project 985 in 2000, Malaysia campus open in 2016, Class A Double First-Class in 2017.

Overseas contact has been part of the university's character from the start, because its founder's own world was the overseas Chinese community, and many early students came from Chinese families in Southeast Asia. It launched an "Overseas Correspondence Courses" programme in 1956 and enrolled its first foreign students in 1981. Current activity includes a programme for innovative talents, run jointly with overseas partners and funded by the China Scholarship Council, and the university has set up 16 Confucius Institutes with partners in 13 countries. One of them operates inside Mae Fah Luang University in Thailand, at that university's Sirindhorn Chinese Language and Culture Center.

Commentators have called XMU Malaysia a historic step, the first big overseas branch ever opened by a Chinese university. Its first chancellor was Professor Wang Ruifang. The university presents the project as faithful to founder Tan Kah Kee's vision. It accepted the Malaysian government's invitation and became the first Chinese university to set up a branch campus in Malaysia. Its stated aim is to be a globally minded university with first-class teaching and research that welcomes cultural diversity.

The campus is in Bandar Serenia, Sepang, in the state of Selangor. It is a 10-minute drive from Kuala Lumpur International Airport and 15 minutes by car from Putrajaya, where the Malaysian government is based.

Some specific partnerships give a flavour of how this works in practice. On 23 May 2016 a delegation from XMU visited the Tokyo Institute of Technology for talks on three themes: how to commercialise research findings, how to deepen ties between universities and industry, and how to get international students interested in the local language and culture.

On 18 November 2016 XMU and Cardiff University in Wales began a strategic partnership. It includes joint supervision of doctoral students and 1.2 million pounds of seed funding for collaborative research projects meant to benefit the Welsh economy. A Cardiff delegation later visited XMU's School of International Relations to look at research collaboration and student exchange.

Visiting students also arrive for recurring China study programmes. Partners in the United States are Eckerd College, Bentley College, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and the Council for Christian Colleges and Universities, and in the Netherlands the partner is University College Utrecht. If you are an exchange student from one of these partners, this is probably the route you will take.

xiamen-university.h: Where you will study: the campuses

blocks.x: Xiamen University works across several sites, and which one you attend depends on your school. Check the university's own admissions pages for the current location of your programme, since schools have moved between campuses over time.

The main campus lies in Siming District on Xiamen Island and covers 167 hectares. It sits at the foot of hills and faces the sea, with Xiamen Bay around it. Most teaching in the arts and humanities, the social sciences, the natural sciences and engineering takes place here. The campus data network is rated the best in the country by scale and level, and serves as a principal node on CERNET2, the national research network.

Haiyun is part of the main campus, near Pearl Bay at the southern end of the city and beside the Xiamen Software Park. Three schools are based here: Software, Information Science and Technology, and Mathematical Sciences.

Xiang'an opened in September 2012, 34 kilometres from the main campus. It was set up with three stated aims. One is to give a home to emerging and applied fields such as bioscience and energy. Another is to offer innovation platforms for applied sciences. The third is to house the southern base of the Confucius Institute.

Over 10,000 students and staff work here, spread over ten units. The Overseas Education College, which looks after international students, is among them, so if you are coming to study Chinese or join a programme for foreign students, this is likely your campus. Health and life science units form the largest group: medicine, pharmaceutical sciences, life sciences, public health and nursing. The rest cover earth sciences, environment and ecology, energy research and aerospace engineering.

The Zhangzhou site occupies 171 hectares inside Zhangzhou's China Merchants development zone, and its buildings echo the style of the main campus. Most of the facilities went to XMU Tan Kah Kee College in July 2012. Then, in September 2020, the newly formed College of Creativity and Innovation arrived and part of the International College returned. Five bodies now share the site: those two colleges, Tan Kah Kee College, the Gulei Petrochemical Research Institute and the Institute of Industrial Technology. Its goals are international cooperation, training of applied talent, turning research into products and attracting talent, and students are encouraged to innovate and start businesses.
XMUM is covered above. It is a separate degree-granting campus in Selangor and a different place from the Chinese sites.
Rankings are one imperfect guide. XMU's position among world rankings is as follows.
341st in the 2026 QS World University Rankings
251st to 300th in the 2026 Times Higher Education world rankings
189th in U.S. News and World Report's 2025 Best Global Universities
101st to 150th worldwide in the 2025 Academic Ranking of World Universities (the Shanghai ranking)
As of 1 September 2017 the university had 20 schools with 44 departments, together with many key research institutes. The list below gives the academic units that were named at that time.
Arts, language and society: Humanities; Foreign Languages and Cultures; Journalism and Communication; Public Affairs; College of Art
Law and economics: School of Law; the Xiamen Academy of International Law; Economics (including the Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics); Management

Natural science and engineering: Chemistry and Chemical Engineering; Mathematics; Oceanography and Environment; Architecture and Civil Engineering; Physics and Mechanical and Electrical Engineering; Electronic Science and Technology
Information technology: Information Science and Technology; Software
Life and medical sciences: Life Science; Pharmaceutical Sciences; the Medical College
Other colleges: Tan Kah Kee College; Overseas Education; Adult Education; Professional Technical; Internet Education
Since the source of this structure dates from 2017, the university may have reorganised since then, so confirm the current list on the official website.
XMU's alumni range from scholars to artists and public figures. Here are the names most often mentioned.
Scholars and thinkers: the economist Gregory Chow, the mathematician Chen Jingrun, and Xie Xide, who led Fudan University from 1983 to 1989
Writers: Lin Yutang (also an inventor), Lu Xun, the Taiwanese poet, critic and teacher Yu Guangzhong, the avant-garde Christian novelist Bei Cun, and the poet and painter Tsai Chih-chan
Music and entertainment: the singer Faye Wong, and the Hong Kong singer and actor Raymond Lam, who studied here for a year in 1996
Business and public life: Wong Ker-lee, a Hong Kong businessman and politician from Fujian; Zhang Gaoli, a former Vice Premier of China's State Council; and Li Wo-shi, magistrate of Kinmen County

Day-to-day life depends largely on the city around the campus, so the rest of this profile looks at Xiamen: where it sits, what the weather does, who lives there, which languages you will hear and how people earn a living.

Xiamen is a sub-provincial city in the southeast of Fujian. Its urban core grew from the old port on the southern part of Xiamen Island, now in Siming District. Today the city also includes Gulangyu Island and a rugged length of mainland coastline. That runs from the Jiulong River's northeastern bank at its western end across to the Xiang'an islands at its eastern end.

The island itself lies roughly one degree above the Tropic of Cancer. Huli District occupies its northern half and Siming District the southern half; Siming also takes in Gulangyu. The mainland part of the city is divided among four districts: Haicang, Jimei, Tong'an and Xiang'an.

In the nineteenth century the harbour on Yundang Bay was counted among the great natural harbours of the world. Land reclamation later filled the mouth of that inlet and turned it into Yundang Lake in Siming, and the municipal government now stands on other reclaimed land beside it.

The nearest point of Lieyu in the Kinmen Islands, which are under Taiwan's administration, is only 6 kilometres off the island. By size it is the fourth largest island in Fujian, and it became a peninsula when a seawall was completed in 1955. The city's waters include Xiamen Port, an outer harbour area, Maluan Bay, Tong'an Bay, the Jiulong River estuary and the channel on the eastern side. Outside the port, Big Kinmen, Little Kinmen, Dadan, Erdan and other islands lie in a row, while Xiamen Island and Gulangyu inside form barriers, so the port is naturally sheltered from storms.

Xiamen has a monsoon-influenced humid subtropical climate, Cfa on the Koppen scale. Summers are long, hot and muggy, though gentler than in most other parts of Fujian, and winters are short, mild and dry.

The hottest month is July, averaging 28.3 degrees Celsius (82.9 F) over a full day, and the coolest is January at 13.1 degrees (55.6 F). Across the whole year the mean is 21.1 degrees (70.0 F). Records kept since 1951 show a low of 0.1 degrees (32 F) on 24 January 2016 and a high of 39.6 degrees (103 F) on 9 August 2019.

Spring is the dampest season in terms of humidity and cloud, but typhoons in late summer and early autumn can leave that stretch of the year wetter in total. Summer and autumn are relatively sunny, and autumn especially is warm and dry. Annual rainfall is 1,301 millimetres (51 inches). Monthly possible sunshine ranges from 29 percent in March to 58 percent in July, giving about 1,893 hours of bright sunshine a year. Frost is very rare. The last snowfall in the city was in January 1893, when snow also fell at Guangzhou, Macau, inland parts of Hong Kong and the hills around Taipei.
Xiamen also has a reputation in China for fairly clean air.

Many of the city's residents are migrants. The census of 2010 counted 3,531,347 people, almost 1.8 times the figure of 2,053,070 recorded in 2000. That is an average annual growth rate of 5.57 percent over the decade. The overall number hides large local jumps, since Jimei District's population quadrupled and Huli District's more than doubled. By the 2020 census the city had 5,163,970 inhabitants. One figure gives 1,967,800 at the end of 2013, another gives 3.73 million for people living there at least half the year, and a further one gives 4,255,000 for December 2014 without saying what counts as a resident. By the end of 2025 the resident population had reached 5.365 million. Most are Han Chinese, with minorities such as the She and Hui.
Mandarin is the official language here, as everywhere in China. Migrants whose families are not Hokkien usually speak Mandarin, their ancestral languages, or both.

The local language is Hokkien, a branch of Southern Min. The Tong'an dialect has the most speakers, the Xiamen dialect is mostly limited to the southwestern part of Xiamen Island, and the Zhangzhou dialect is spoken in part of Haicang District. Several English words come from local Hokkien, among them Amoy, tea, cumshaw, pekoe, kowtow and ketchup.

Evidence of organised religion in the area goes back to the Sui dynasty, when Buddhism reached the Tong'an area. It spread to Xiamen Island in the Tang dynasty. By the nineteenth century the city proper had two Dutch Reformed churches and two London Missionary Society churches, and on the island there were three further Dutch Reformed missions, at Kang-thau, Kio-than and Chhan-chhu-oa.

xiamen-university.h: Work, industry and the local economy

blocks.x: Xiamen has a varied and well-developed economy, and it matters to students because internship, graduate-job and start-up opportunities follow the local industries. The city was the first in China to use the World Bank's business environment indicators with the aim of building a first-rate business climate. In 2018 the National Development and Reform Commission ranked it second among the 22 cities it evaluated, and it was seen as a national leader in handling construction permits, getting electricity and cross-border trade. Its overall credit index in 2018 was second among 36 provincial capitals and sub-provincial cities.

The Siming and Huli districts together form the Special Economic Zone. Five industries get the most attention: financial services, modern logistics, tourism and culture, equipment manufacturing and electronic information.
Since reform and opening up began four decades ago, the city's GDP has grown by an average of 15.4 percent each year. Key 2018 figures were these.
Per capita GDP of 118,015 yuan (US$17,105)
Per capita disposable income of 50,948 yuan
Public budget revenue of 128.3 billion yuan
1,626 high-tech enterprises, which is 44 percent of Fujian's total
Total foreign trade of 600.5 billion yuan, with dependence on foreign trade at 125 percent

By the end of 2018 the city had attracted 14,818 foreign-invested projects. Contracted foreign investment totalled 66 billion dollars and actual investment 37.9 billion. Sixty-two overseas Fortune 500 companies had invested in 112 projects. A city government forecast made in 2023 aims for GDP per capita of US$25,000.

Each year in early September the city stages the China International Fair for Investment and Trade, an event meant to bring foreign direct investment into mainland China. It also hosts the annual Straits Forum, whose 2019 edition ran from 15 to 21 June and drew more than 10,000 people.

Banking is highly developed. The biggest bank is a state-owned commercial bank. Others include Xiamen International Bank, a Sino-foreign joint venture, Xiamen Bank, which is entirely foreign-funded, and Xiamen Rural Commercial Bank. Several foreign banks have representative offices in the city.

Haicang Investment Zone lies to the southeast of the island, where the Xiamen, Zhangzhou and Quanzhou delta ends, facing the island across a narrow channel. Zhangzhou borders it on the west and Jimei on the north. Covering 100 square kilometres, it is the biggest national zone for Taiwanese investors, approved by the State Council in 1989, and sits near Xiamen Port. It aims to become a new port area, new industrial area and sub-centre of greater Xiamen. It has four functional areas: the Haicang Port Area, Xinyang Industrial Area, Southern Industrial Area and Haicang New Urban Area.

The Xiamen section of the China (Fujian) Pilot Free Trade Zone lies in the northwest of the city around Dongdu port, near National Road 319 and the Yingxia railway, and is linked to Gaoqi International Airport. The State Council approved a 5 square kilometre zone on 15 October 1992; the first phase, 0.63 square kilometres, began operating on 28 November 1993. It is described as the most modern international logistics zone in southeastern China.

The Torch high-tech zone dates from 1990, when the former State Scientific and Technological Commission and the city government set it up together. It has since grown into a single zone made up of several parks. Dell, ABB, Panasonic, FDK, Xiamen Tungaloy and Fujitsu are all enlarging their operations there, and the American firm Bourns Inc. judged it the best place in China for foreign investors. It focuses on information technology, biotechnology, new energy, new materials, oceanology, advanced manufacturing and environmental technology. Exports go mainly to the US, Japan, Southeast Asia, Western Europe, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, and include computers, colour monitors, microscopes, power supplies, integrated circuits, stepping motors, wireless telephones, switching equipment and tungsten carbide micro-drills.
The output figures below are for 2018, so treat them as a snapshot rather than current numbers.

Panel displays: the city is among the Chinese regions where TFT liquid crystal display production has grown fastest. Its scale ranks sixth nationally, it is the only pilot city for a national optoelectronic display cluster, and it has the world's largest R&D and production base for touch screen modules. Output reached 131.5 billion yuan with a complete industrial chain. The parks are the Xiamen Tongan Xiang'an Hi-tech Industrial Base and the Xiamen Torch Hi-Tech Industrial Zone (Xiang'an).

Computers and communications equipment: factories turn out finished computers, mobile phones, phone camera lenses, micro motors, flexible circuit boards, Bluetooth and wireless access devices and positioning sensors, alongside suppliers of components, accessories, peripherals and IT services. The complete-machine brands have global influence. Output was 120.4 billion yuan (US$17.68 billion), in the same two parks.

Semiconductors and integrated circuits: more than 200 IC companies form a chain covering design, manufacturing, testing, equipment and materials, and applications. Output was 41.7 billion yuan (US$6.11 billion). The parks are the Xiang'an Hi-tech Industrial Base, the Science and Technology Innovation Park, the Haicang Information Industrial Park and the IC Strait Free Trade Zone Industrial Base.

Software and information services: the sector spans the platform economy, industrial software, animation and games, cloud computing and information security, and Xiamen has been awarded the label of a distinctive software city of China. Output was 149.3 billion yuan (US$21.78 billion), 67 percent of it from Xiamen Software Park.

Machinery and equipment: it covers large and medium passenger buses, engineering machinery, shipbuilding, aviation maintenance, and equipment for power transmission and distribution. Output was 103.7 billion yuan (US$15.13 billion). The parks include the Machinery Industry Concentration Area, the Torch Power Transmission and Distribution Industry Base, the Haicang Ship Industrial Zone, the Aviation Industrial Zone and the Airport Industrial Zone.

New materials: special metals and advanced polymers dominate, including photoelectric information materials, new energy, energy-saving and environmental materials and advanced carbon nanomaterials. Output was 88.9 billion yuan (US$12.95 billion), in the Xiang'an base and the Torch zone at Xiang'an.

Titles the city has won include best tourist city in China, national model city for tourism and leisure, and one of the country's most romantic leisure cities. Holiday popularity and visitor satisfaction have long been among the best nationally, inbound tourism and foreign exchange earnings rank in the national top 10, and more people travel to Taiwan through Xiamen Port than through any other Chinese port.

The exhibition business is large. In 2018 the city held 229 exhibitions across 2.38 million square metres, up 8.6 percent on the previous year. Hotels and conference centres hosted 9,262 commercial meetings of more than 50 people, up 12.1 percent. Total attendance of 1.88 million from China and abroad rose by 12.1 percent, and revenue came to 40.3 billion yuan (US$5.86 billion). Venues include the Xiamen International Conference and Exhibition Center, the Xiamen International Conference Center and the Fliport Conference and Exhibition Center, and an east sports exhibition area was under construction.

In creative design, film and high-end art, the city has grown quickly. Xiamen was one of the first designated National Culture Export Bases, and it hosts the third Red Dot Design Museum in the world. The Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival, a major event in Chinese cinema, is scheduled to come to the city every second year for a decade starting in 2019. Culture and creative industries earned 104 billion yuan (US$15.13 billion) in 2018. The parks include a national demonstration base for integrating culture with science and technology, the National Fujian and Taiwan Cultural Industry Experimental Park, the Longshan Cultural and Creative Industrial Park, the Huli Creative Industrial Park, the Jimei film and television industrial park, the Tong'an Cultural Industrial Park and the Cross-Straits Architectural Design Cultural and Creative Park.
In summary, Xiamen offers a mild coastal setting, a very international outlook and strong electronics, software and services sectors, which is a useful mix for students.

xiamen-university.h: How to apply, step by step

blocks.x: The process below is the general route for international degree applicants to Chinese universities. Xiamen University may add its own forms, interviews or deadlines, which a CAS advisor confirms before you apply.
Choose a program and check its language of instruction, duration and annual tuition on the Programs tab.

Check the admission requirements: a valid foreign passport, good health, and the right previous qualification (high-school graduation for a bachelor's degree, a bachelor's degree for a master's, a master's degree for a doctorate).
Bachelor's applicants take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) and send the result with the application.
Prove language ability: an HSK certificate for Chinese-taught programs, or English test results (for example IELTS or TOEFL) for English-taught programs, unless you studied in English.
Prepare certified transcripts and diplomas, a physical examination form, a police clearance certificate and a study plan or personal statement where the program asks for them.
Apply online through the university's international student system, or let CAS prepare and submit the application for you, and pay the application fee.
After admission you receive an admission notice and a JW202 or JW201 form, which you take to the Chinese embassy or consulate to apply for an X1 (long-term study) visa.
Travel to Xiamen, register at Xiamen University by the date in the admission notice, and convert your entry visa into a residence permit within 30 days of arrival.
The Xiamen University of Technology (XMUT; Chinese: 厦门理工学院; lit. 'Xiamen Polytechnic College') is a provincial public university located in Xiamen, Fujian, China.

Founded in 1981, at around the same time as the Xiamen Special Economic Zone, it was originally known as Lujiang Industrial University. the university status was conferred by Xi Jinping, current General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party, when he was Governor of Fujian Province. It is a public university which since 2013 has been jointly administered by Xiamen City Government and Fujian Provincial Government, at which time it was also designated a "key provincial university".
The university has created a joint-venture called Digital Innovation College with partnering universities; Ming Chuan University and Central University.

The university's main campus is located in Jimei District, although it continues to maintain a smaller campus in downtown Xiamen's Siming District. The combined campus area is more than 120 hectares. (24.621963°N 118.086333°E﻿ / 24.621963; 118.086333﻿ (Jimei campus)).
XMUT has a total enrollment of 21,000 domestic students. In addition, since the 1990s it has hosted international students from all over the world.
The university currently offers 63 undergraduate and graduate programs.
It currently has around 1000 faculty members, including approximately 50 overseas teachers.

XMUT currently has cooperation agreements with more than 30 universities and corporations in over 20 countries. It offers more than 20 programs which allow credit transfer in partnership with 10 overseas universities, and offers joint degrees at undergraduate and graduate level in cooperation with universities in Britain, Canada, the United States, Malaysia and the Philippines. In addition, XMUT has cooperation agreements with 18 institutes of higher education in Taiwan.
In 2008 XMUT was named as one of the "Top Ten Fastest Growing Universities in China".

Since 2010 it has been one of only three universities in Fujian to be part of the Ministry of Education-sponsored  "Outstanding Engineers' Training Program", and the only university in Fujian to be part of the Ministry of Science and Technology's "Innovation Engineering Program". In 2011 it also became the only university in Fujian to win the "National Innovation and Entrepreneurship Education Award".

Most of what students need to know about daily life comes down to the city around the campus: its climate, how people get around, and what there is to do. The following sections describe Xiamen, where Xiamen University of Technology is located.

Xiamen is a sub-provincial city in southeastern Fujian whose urban core grew up from the port of Xiamen on southern Xiamen Island, now located within Siming District. It now also includes Gulangyu Island and the rugged coast of the mainland from the northeast bank of the Jiulong River in the west to the islands of Xiang'an in the east. Xiamen Island lies about one degree north of the Tropic of Cancer. It is divided between Huli District in the north and Siming District in the south. Siming also includes Gulangyu. Its mainland territory is divided among Haicang, Jimei, Tong'an, and Xiang'an districts.

In the 19th century, Xiamen's harbor on Yundang Bay was considered one of the world's great natural harbors. Land reclamation has since been used to fill in the mouth of this inlet, turning it into Siming District's Yundang Lake. The municipal government is located on other reclaimed land beside it.
The nearest point of Liehyu in the Kinmen Islands, Republic of China (Taiwan), lies only 6 kilometers (4 mi) off Xiamen Island.

Xiamen Island is the fourth largest island in Fujian province. It became a peninsula after the completion of the seawall in 1955. Xiamen waters include Xiamen Port, Outer Harbor Area, Maluan Bay, Tongan Bay, Jiulong River's estuary area and the waterway on the east side. Outside the Xiamen Port, Big Kinmen, Little Kinmen, Dadan, Erdan and other island are arranged in a horizontal line. Inside, it has Xiamen Island, Gulangyu Island and other island barriers, making it a good natural port protected from storms.

Xiamen has a monsoonal humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa), characterised by long, hot and humid summers (but moderate compared to much of the rest of the province) and short, mild and dry winters. The warmest month is July, with a 24-hour average of 28.3 °C (82.9 °F), and the coolest month is January, averaging 13.1 °C (55.6 °F); the annual mean is 21.1 °C (70.0 °F). Extremes since 1951 have ranged from 0.1 °C (32 °F) on 24 January 2016 to 39.6 °C (103 °F) on 9 August 2019. Spring, both by humidity and percentage of sunshine, is the dampest season but typhoons in late summer and early autumn can make the latter period wetter overall. Summer and autumn are marked by comparatively sunny conditions, while autumn is warm and dry. The annual rainfall is 1,301 millimeters (51 in). With monthly percent possible sunshine ranging from 29% in March to 58% in July, the city receives 1,893 hours of bright sunshine annually. Frost occurs very rarely, and the last snowfall in the city took place in January 1893, when snow also fell at Guangzhou, Macau, in the inland parts of Hong Kong and in the hills of Taipei.
The area is known within China for its relatively low pollution.
A large number of the populace are migrants.

In 1910, Xue Zidao (薛子道), a 9-year-old boy was reported to have fathered a child with Li Fuzhen (李福珍), an 8-year-old girl. These are considered the youngest recorded parents in combined age. According to a 1957 Ripley's publication, the family name was Hsi and they were farmers.

According to the 2020 Census, Xiamen has a population of 5,163,970 inhabitants. According to the 2010 Census, Xiamen has a population of 3,531,347 inhabitants, almost 1.8 times the population counted for the last census in 2000 (which was of 2,053,070 inhabitants). The annual average population growth was of 5.57% for the period 2000–2010. This masks the population explosion in Jimei District, however, which quadrupled since the prior census; Huli District's population more than doubled. The resident population was 1,967,800 in 2013 yearend, and with a population of 3.73 million (those residing at least half a year). The total resident population is said to be 4,255,000 in December 2014, without specifying what counts as a resident.
By the end of 2025, the resident population of Xiamen has reached 5.365 million, the majority being Han people. There are also some ethnic minorities such as She and Hui.
As with all of China, the official language is Mandarin. Migrants of non-Hokkien ancestry usually speak Mandarin and/or their ancestral tongues.

The indigenous language is Hokkien, a subgroup of Southern Min, with the Tong'an dialect being the most populous and prevalent. The Xiamen dialect is mostly confined to the southwest quarter of Xiamen Island, while the Zhangzhou dialect is spoken in a section of Haicang District.
The English words "Amoy", "tea" (Chinese: 茶; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: tê), "cumshaw" (感謝; kám-siā), "pekoe" (白毫; pe̍h-hô), kowtow (磕頭; khàu-thâu), and "ketchup" (鮭汁; koê-chiap) are derived from the local Hokkien.

The first evidence of organised religion existed in the area was dated to Sui dynasty when Buddhism was first spread to Tong'an region and spread to Xiamen Island during Tang dynasty. In the 19th century, Xiamen proper had two Dutch Reformed and two LMS churches. Xiamen Island was home to three Dutch Reformed missions at "Kang-thau", "Kio-than", and "Chhan-chhu-oa".

Xiamen has a diverse and well-developed economy. It is the first to refer to the business environment indexes of the World Bank with the aim of creating world's first-rated business environment. In 2018, its business environment ranked 2nd among 22 cities across the country that was evaluated by the National Development and Reform Commission. Its measures in areas such as dealing with construction permits, getting electricity, and trading across borders take the lead in the country.
Its social credit system has been improved. In 2018, its overall credit index ranked 2nd among 36 provincial capitals and sub-provincial cities and above.
The Siming and Huli districts form its Special Economic Zone.
Xiamen focuses on the development of five major industries – electronic information, equipment manufacturing, tourism and culture, modern logistics, and financial services.

Xiamen's GDP has grown at an average annual rate of 15.4 percent since China's reform and opening-up four decades ago. In 2018, per capita GDP: 118,015 yuan ($17,105); per capita disposable income: 50,948 yuan; public financial budget revenue: 128.3 billion yuan; 1,626 hi-tech enterprises, accounting for 44 percent of the total number of Fujian province; 600.5 billion yuan of total foreign trade value; degree of dependence on foreign trade has reached 125 percent.

By the end of 2018, Xiamen brought in a total of 14,818 foreign-invested projects; contractual foreign investments: $66 billion, actual foreign investments: $37.9 billion; 62 overseas Fortune 500 companies invested in 112 projects in Xiamen.
Xiamen is also the host of the China International Fair for Investment and Trade held annually in early September to attract foreign direct investment into mainland China.
Xiamen also hold Straits Forum annually. The 2019 edition kicked off in the coastal city from 15 to 21 June. More than 10,000 people attended the annual forum this year.
In 2023 forecast by the city government, Xiamen is aiming for 25,000 of GDP per capita measured by USD.

Xiamen has highly developed banking services. The biggest bank is the state-owned commercial bank, Sino-foreign joint venture Xiamen International Bank, solely foreign-funded Xiamen Bank, and Xiamen Rural Commercial Bank.
Various foreign banks that have established representative offices in Xiamen.

Haicang Investment Zone (廈門海滄台商資區区) is situated to the southeast of Xiamen Island, at the tip of the Xiamen-Zhangzhou-Quanzhou Delta in South Fujian bordering Zhangzhou City to the west, Jimei District to the north, and overlooking Xiamen Island across the narrow water. The 100-square-kilometer Haicang Investment Zone is the largest national investment zone for Taiwan business people authorized by the State Council in 1989. It is situated close to Xiamen Port. The zone aims at becoming a new port area, a new industrial area and a sub-center of greater Xiamen in the 21st century. It is divided into the following four functional areas in line with its overall plan: Haicang Port Area, Xinyang Industrial Area, Southern Industrial Area and Haicang New Urban Area.

Xiamen Area of China (Fujian) Pilot Free Trade Zone (福建自贸试验区厦门片区管委会) is located in the northwest part of Xiamen, within the area of Dongdu port. Near No 319 national road and Yingxia railway, it is connected with Gaoqi International Airport. On 15 October 1992, the State Council approved establishment of the zone with an area of 5 square kilometers; the first phase covers 0.63 square kilometers and was put into operation on 28 November 1993. It is the most modern international logistics zone in the southeast part of China.

Xiamen Torch Development Zone for High Technology Industries (厦门火炬高新区管委会) was jointly established by the former State Scientific and Technological Commission and the Xiamen municipal government in 1990 and has gradually developed into "one zone with multi parks". A favorable investment environment and high returns has made the zone into a hot spot for foreign investment. Bourns Inc. of the United States concluded the zone the most ideal target for foreign investors in China. Some of the world's top 500 companies such as Dell, ABB Switch, ABB Low-Voltage, ABB High-Voltage, Panasonic, FDK, Xiamen Tungaloy, and Fujitsu are rapidly expanding their operations in Xiamen. The zone is oriented towards information technology, biotechnology, new energy, new materials, oceanology, advanced manufacturing, and environment technology. Most of its exports go to countries and areas such as the US, Japan, Southeast Asia, West Europe, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. Hi-tech exports include computers, color monitors, microscopes, power supply units, integrated circuits, stepping motors, wireless telephones, switching equipment, tungsten carbide micro-drills, and similar products.

Xiamen is one of China's regions with rapid development of the TFT liquid crystal display (LCD) industry. Its industrial scale ranks sixth in the country and is the only pilot city with a national optoelectronic display industrial cluster. The city also has the largest R&D and production base of touch screen modules in the world. Xiamen's panel display industry reached an output value of 131.5 billion yuan in 2018, forming a complete industrial chain layout. Industrial parks include Xiamen Tongan Xiang'an Hi-tech Industrial Base and Xiamen Torch Hi-Tech Industrial Zone (Xiang'an).

Xiamen has gathered integrated manufacturing enterprises in such fields as complete computers, mobile phones, mobile phone lenses, micro motors, flexible circuit boards, bluetooth and wireless access equipment, and positioning and navigation sensors, as well assupporting enterprises of basic components, accessories, external equipment and IT services. The complete machine brand has global influence. The industry reached an output value of 120.4 billion yuan ($17.68 billion) in 2018. Industrial parks include Xiamen Tongan Xiang'an Hi-tech Industrial Base and Xiamen Torch Hi-Tech Industrial Zone (Xiang'an).

Xiamen is home to more than 200 integrated circuit (IC) enterprises which form an industrial chain covering IC design, manufacturing, testing, equipment and materials as well as applications. Xiamen's IC industry reached an output value of 41.7 billion yuan ($6.11 billion) in 2018. Industrial parks include Xiamen Tongan Xiang'an Hi-tech Industrial Base, Xiamen Science and Technology Innovation Park, Xiamen Haicang Information Industrial Park, and Xiamen IC Strait Free Trade Zone Industrial Base.

The software and information services industry in Xiamen covers various fields including the platform economy, industrial application software, animation and games and cloud computing and information security. The city has won the title of "China's Characteristic City in Software". The industrial output value of Xiamen's software and information services industry in 2018 reached 149.3 billion yuan ($21.78 billion), with Xiamen Software Park accounting for 67 percent of that figure.

Xiamen's machinery and equipment industry covers five industrial sectors – large and medium-sized passenger cars, power transmission and distribution equipment, aviation maintenance, engineering machinery and shipbuilding, with an output value of 103.7 billion yuan ($15.13 billion) in 2018. Industrial parks include Xiamen Machinery industry concentration area, Xiamen Torch Power Transmission and Distribution Industry Base, Xiamen Haicang Ship Industrial Zone, Xiamen Aviation Industrial Zone, and Xiamen Airport Industrial Zone.

Xiamen's new materials industry is dominated by special metal materials and advanced polymer materials, including photoelectric information materials, new energy, energy saving and environmental protection materials, and advanced carbon nanomaterials. The industry reached an output value of 88.9 billion yuan ($12.95 billion) in 2018. Industrial parks include Xiamen Tongan Xiang'an Hi-tech Industrial Base and Xiamen Torch Hi-Tech Industrial Zone (Xiang'an).

Xiamen has been honored as the Top Tourist City in China, a Demonstration City of Tourism and Leisure in China and one of China's most romantic leisure cities. The holiday tourism popularity and tourist satisfaction in Xiamen has long been at the forefront in China, and its inbound tourism and foreign exchange earnings have been ranked in China's top 10. The number of people going to Taiwan via Xiamen Port ranks first in China.

In 2018, Xiamen held a total of 229 exhibitions, with a total exhibition area of 2.38 million square meters, up 8.6 percent year-on-year. The hotels and conference centers in the city hosted 9,262 commercial meetings with more than 50 people attending, up 12.1 percent year-on-year. The total number of participants from home and abroad to Xiamen reached 1.88 million, with a year-on-year increase of 12.1 percent. The total revenue of the exhibition industry in Xiamen reached 40.3 billion yuan ($5.86 billion). Industrial parks include Xiamen International Conference & Exhibition Center, Xiamen International Conference Center, Xiamen Fliport Conference & Exhibition Center, and Xiamen east sports exhibition area (under construction).

Xiamen has seen rapid development in creative design, the film industry and high-end artworks in recent years. The city was listed among the first National Culture Export Bases and is home to the world's third Red Dot Design Museum. Also, the Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival, one of the top events in China's film industry, is to be presented in Xiamen once every two years for the 10 years following 2019. The total revenue of Xiamen's culture and creativity industry reached 104 billion yuan ($15.13 billion) in 2018. Industrial parks include National demonstration base for the integration of culture and science and technology, National Fujian and Taiwan cultural industry experimental park, Longshan cultural and creative industrial park, Huli creative industrial park, Jimeiji film and television industrial park, Tongan cultural industrial park, and Cross-Straits architectural design cultural and creative park.
Xiamen University of Technology lists 54 programs for international students on this site: 3 bachelor, 51 master's programs.

By language of instruction: 28 taught in Chinese, 26 taught in English. English-taught programs do not require Chinese to start; for Chinese-taught programs you normally need an HSK certificate at the level the program sets.
